- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after recent highs and underestimates after recent lows.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, suggesting lag or delayed adjustment to true market dynamics.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in price after a spike; often continues to forecast upward even when true price starts to fall.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lagged response to recent history rather than real-time adaptation.
- Model underestimates price drops after a spike, especially when the spike is followed by a sharp correction.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating sharp drops and overestimating gradual declines.
